# Enforced rules

This catalog lists each rule that a gate enforces. A script makes it from the rule sources, so it cannot drift from them.

- A reviewer does not report a violation of a rule here. The gate already fails on it.
- [code-style.md](./code-style.md) holds the rules, with the rules that only a reviewer enforces.
- [gate-design.md](./gate-design.md) tells which gate a new rule gets, and holds the queue of rules with no gate yet.

When you add, remove or change a rule in `.oxlintrc.json`, a JS plugin, a tsconfig, `package.json` or `.github/workflows/check.yml`, run `pnpm rules:catalog`. `pnpm check:rules-catalog` fails while this file is stale.

## Lint rules: oxlint built-ins

`pnpm lint` fails on each rule below. A type-aware rule reads the type of an expression through tsgolint (rung 2 in gate-design.md). A rule applies to each file that `pnpm lint` reads, unless the scope tells otherwise. The reason is the comment above the key in `.oxlintrc.json`. Rules that share one comment share one row.

The config also keeps oxlint's default `correctness` category on, at `warn`. `pnpm lint` runs with `--deny-warnings`, so those rules also fail the gate. This table lists only the rules that the config names.

| Rules | Type-aware | Scope | Options | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`import/default`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/import/default.html) | no |  |  | import/default: a default import from a module that has no default export. |
| [`import/namespace`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/import/namespace.html) | no |  |  | import/namespace: `ns.x` on a namespace import whose module does not export `x`. |
| [`import/no-cycle`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/import/no-cycle.html) | no |  |  | import/no-cycle: a module that reaches itself again through its imports. ESM loads a cycle without an error, but a binding read during module evaluation can be in its TDZ, and the order of `export` lines then decides whether the process boots. It resolves relative and `@warden/*` specifiers alike. It skips type-only imports, the inline `{ type X }` form too, although that form keeps a runtime import under verbatimModuleSyntax. Break a cycle by moving the shared piece into a module that both sides import, or by importing a concrete sibling instead of a barrel. |
| [`no-console`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/eslint/no-console.html) | no | Off in `**/scripts/**`, `.claude/hooks/**` |  | `warden mcp` speaks JSON-RPC over stdio, so a stray console.log in product code corrupts the protocol stream. Product code writes through process.stdout/stderr on purpose; scripts are exempt below. |
| [`no-empty`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/eslint/no-empty.html) | no |  |  | no-empty: an empty block, an empty `catch {}` included (`allowEmptyCatch` stays false). A `catch` handles the failure, logs safe fields, or holds a comment that says why the failure is safe to drop. A comment inside the block counts as content. |
| [`node/no-process-env`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/node/no-process-env.html) | no | Off in `packages/env/src/**`; `**/scripts/**`, `.claude/hooks/**` |  | Read configuration through @warden/env (docs/environment.md), never process.env. packages/env is the owner and is exempt below. A deliberate exception elsewhere takes `// oxlint-disable-next-line node/no-process-env -- <why>`. |
| [`preserve-caught-error`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/eslint/preserve-caught-error.html) | no |  |  | A `catch` that throws a new error must pass the caught one as `{ cause }`, so the stack and the original failure survive the rewrap. Default options. |
| [`typescript/await-thenable`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/await-thenable.html) | yes |  |  | await-thenable: an `await` of a value that is not a promise. Remove the `await`. |
| [`typescript/consistent-type-imports`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/consistent-type-imports.html) | no |  | `{"disallowTypeAnnotations":false,"fixStyle":"inline-type-imports"}` | consistent-type-imports: an import used only as a type, including only inside `typeof`, takes `type`. `verbatimModuleSyntax` already fails `tsc` on a type imported without it, but a value imported only for `typeof` compiles and stays in the runtime import graph. `fixStyle` matches the tree: a mixed import marks each type inline. The fixer then writes `import { type X }` for a declaration whose every name is a type; rewrite that as `import type { X }`, because the inline form keeps a side-effect import of the module. `disallowTypeAnnotations` is off: an `import("…")` type is erased, so it costs nothing at runtime. |
| [`typescript/no-array-delete`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-array-delete.html) | yes |  |  | no-array-delete: `delete xs[i]` leaves a hole. Use `splice` or `filter`. |
| [`typescript/no-base-to-string`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-base-to-string.html) | yes |  |  | no-base-to-string: `String(v)` or a template on a value that may be an object prints `[object Object]`. Narrow the value at its boundary, or pick the text you mean (`JSON.stringify` of a JSON value, `error.message`). |
| [`typescript/no-deprecated`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-deprecated.html) | yes |  |  | no-deprecated: a use of a symbol whose declaration carries `@deprecated`, from a dependency (zod 4, the AI SDK, the TypeScript API, drizzle, the MCP SDK) or from this repo. A deprecated API works today, and the next major version removes it. Migrate to the replacement the tag names. A site that must keep the old symbol carries a directive with the reason (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts` keeps the low-level MCP `Server`). |
| [`typescript/no-duplicate-type-constituents`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-duplicate-type-constituents.html) | yes |  |  | no-duplicate-type-constituents: a union or intersection that repeats a member. It also reports `\| undefined` on an optional PARAMETER; an optional property keeps it, because `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is on. |
| [`typescript/no-explicit-any`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-explicit-any.html) | no |  |  | no-explicit-any: write `unknown` plus a parse, never `any`. |
| [`typescript/no-floating-promises`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-floating-promises.html), [`typescript/no-misused-promises`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-misused-promises.html) | yes |  |  | no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises: an unawaited promise drops its error, and an `async` callback where a void callback is expected rejects unhandled. Await it, return it, or spell fire-and-forget as `void`. |
| [`typescript/no-for-in-array`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-for-in-array.html) | yes |  |  | no-for-in-array: `for…in` over an array walks string keys. Use `for…of`. |
| [`typescript/no-implied-eval`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-implied-eval.html) | yes |  |  | no-implied-eval: a string passed to `setTimeout` / `new Function` is `eval`. Pass a function. |
| [`typescript/no-meaningless-void-operator`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-meaningless-void-operator.html) | yes |  |  | no-meaningless-void-operator: `void` on an expression that is already `void`. |
| [`typescript/no-misused-spread`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-misused-spread.html) | yes |  |  | no-misused-spread: a spread of a string, a promise, or a class instance. Split a string into code points with `Array.from`, which states the intent. |
| [`typescript/no-non-null-assertion`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-non-null-assertion.html) | no |  |  | no-non-null-assertion: a postfix `!` is a runtime promise the compiler cannot keep. Keep the narrowing instead (destructure, `.at(-1)` plus a check, `for…of` over `entries()`, a local). When absence is impossible, throw an `Error` that names the invariant; when it is possible, handle it. Never trade `!` for `as T`. Scripts included, no override. |
| [`typescript/no-redundant-type-constituents`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-redundant-type-constituents.html) | yes |  |  | no-redundant-type-constituents: a union member another member absorbs (`unknown \| X`, `"a" \| string`). Write the wide type and say the rest in the doc comment, or derive the exact union. |
| [`typescript/no-unnecessary-condition`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-unnecessary-condition.html) | yes |  | `{"allowConstantLoopConditions":"only-allowed-literals"}` | no-unnecessary-condition: a condition, `?.`, or `??` whose result the types already decide. Delete it only when a parse or the code above it established the type. When the value comes from JSON, an SDK, env, a cast, or a child process, fix the type at that boundary instead: a zod parse, `.at(i)` for an index read in `scripts/` (which has no `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`), or a `T \| undefined` type. TS does not see a write inside a callback or through a shared object, so a flag set that way keeps its check with `// oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-unnecessary-condition -- <reason>`; a security or fail-closed guard does too. `allowConstantLoopConditions: "only-allowed-literals"` allows the literal `while (true)`, the loop the tree uses; a variable of type `true` as a loop condition still fails. It applies to every surface, JavaScript included. |
| [`typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion.html) | yes |  |  | no-unnecessary-type-assertion: an `as T` or `<T>` that does not change the type, an `as T` where the context already expects `T` and the value fits it, and a `!` on a value that is never null or undefined. Delete the assertion; when it was the only place a reader learned the type, annotate the binding or the return type instead. A comment that explained the deleted cast goes with it. It applies to every surface, with no override. |
| [`typescript/no-unsafe-argument`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-argument.html), [`typescript/no-unsafe-assignment`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-assignment.html), [`typescript/no-unsafe-call`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-call.html), [`typescript/no-unsafe-member-access`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-member-access.html), [`typescript/no-unsafe-return`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-return.html) | yes | Off in `**/*.mjs`, `**/*.js`, `**/*.cjs` |  | The no-unsafe-* family, all five members: an `any` may not flow into a return, an argument, a call, a member read, or an assignment. Type external, persisted, and protocol data as `unknown` and parse it at the owning boundary (docs/conventions.md §2) instead of letting `any` carry it on. Do not swap the `any` for an `as T`: give the value a type that it provably has. The usual sources and their fixes: `JSON.parse` (bind it as `unknown`, or parse it with a zod schema), `Array.isArray` on `unknown` (an `isUnknownArray` guard, or a `: unknown` binding for the element), `Object.entries` on `object` (`Object.keys` plus `Reflect.get` into `unknown`), a Node stream or `events.once` (`text()` from `node:stream/consumers`, or an `unknown[]` binding), and `await import()` of a runtime path (a static import). The family is off for JavaScript sources in the last "overrides" entry; JSDoc-typed `.mjs` is `any` by construction. |
| [`typescript/no-unsafe-type-assertion`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-type-assertion.html) | yes |  |  | no-unsafe-type-assertion: an `as T` (or a JSDoc cast) where `T` is narrower than the type of the value. The compiler then accepts a claim that no code checks. Fix in this order: delete the cast; parse the value at its owning boundary with zod, and reuse the schema that already exists (`packages/core/src/schema.ts` and its neighbours); narrow with a guard (`isRecord` and `errnoCode` in `packages/core/src/guards.ts`, or a `value is T` predicate). Where a parse can fail on a hot or security path, use `safeParse` and the path's existing degraded or unverified result, not a new throw. Keep a cast only for an SDK type gap or a generic walker, with `// oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-unsafe-type-assertion -- <reason>`. Never `as unknown as T` (`anti-slop/no-chained-type-assertions`). It applies to every surface, JavaScript included, with no override. |
| [`typescript/no-unsafe-unary-minus`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-unary-minus.html) | yes |  |  | no-unsafe-unary-minus: unary minus on a value that is not a number or bigint. |
| [`typescript/no-useless-default-assignment`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/no-useless-default-assignment.html) | yes |  |  | no-useless-default-assignment: a default for a binding that is never `undefined`. Delete the default, or widen the type if `undefined` can arrive. |
| [`typescript/only-throw-error`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/only-throw-error.html) | yes |  |  | only-throw-error: a `throw` of a value that is not an `Error` has no stack and no `message`. Throw an `Error` (or a subclass). A caught `unknown` may be rethrown as it is (the rule's defaults). |
| [`typescript/require-array-sort-compare`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/require-array-sort-compare.html) | yes |  |  | require-array-sort-compare: `.sort()` with no comparator orders numbers, tuples and objects by their string form. Pass a comparator. `ignoreStringArrays` stays on (its default): a `string[]` sorts by UTF-16 code unit, which is deterministic. |
| [`typescript/restrict-template-expressions`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/restrict-template-expressions.html) | yes |  |  | restrict-template-expressions: an array or object in a template literal prints `a,b` or `[object Object]`. |
| [`typescript/return-await`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/return-await.html) | yes |  | `"error-handling-correctness-only"` | return-await, correctness option only: a promise returned without `await` inside a `try` (or a `catch` that has a `finally`) settles after the block exits, so its `catch` never sees the rejection and its `finally` runs too early. Write `return await`. The default option also asks for style edits outside a `try`, and those change no behavior. |
| [`typescript/switch-exhaustiveness-check`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/switch-exhaustiveness-check.html) | yes |  | `{"considerDefaultExhaustiveForUnions":true}` | switch-exhaustiveness-check: a switch over a union with no `default` covers every member. A `default` counts as exhaustive; end it in `assertNever` (packages/core/src/assert-never.ts), which review checks. |
| [`typescript/unbound-method`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/unbound-method.html) | yes |  |  | unbound-method: a method read as a value loses `this`. Bind it or wrap it in an arrow; declare a member that never reads `this` as a function-typed property. |
| [`unicorn/no-useless-spread`](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/unicorn/no-useless-spread.html) | no |  |  | no-useless-spread: `{ ...{ a } }` is `{ a }`, and `[...[a]]` is `[a]`. |

## Lint rules: `anti-slop` plugin

`pnpm lint` fails on each rule below. The description is the rule's own `meta.docs.description`. `pnpm check:oxlint-plugin` drives each rule through the root config.

| Rule | Scope | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anti-slop/no-chained-type-assertions` |  | Disallow chained TypeScript as and angle-bracket assertions, including parenthesized chains. |
| `anti-slop/no-module-mocking` |  | Disallow Vitest and Jest module mocking; tests must replace dependencies through real interfaces. |
| `anti-slop/no-object-parameters` |  | Disallow object function parameters; inputs must use an owner-provided type and be parsed at their boundary. |
| `anti-slop/no-reflect-apply` |  | Disallow Reflect.apply; call typed functions directly or model dynamic dispatch behind an interface. |
| `anti-slop/no-unknown-type-aliases` |  | Disallow type aliases whose resolved type is unknown; unknown must remain visible at an allowed boundary. |
| `anti-slop/no-widen-then-assert` |  | Disallow local const flows that explicitly widen a known value before asserting the widened binding to a narrower type. |

## Lint rules: `warden` plugin

`pnpm lint` fails on each rule below. The description is the rule's own `meta.docs.description`. `pnpm check:oxlint-plugin` drives each rule through the root config.

| Rule | Scope | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `warden/no-exported-hasher` |  | Disallow exporting a function whose parameter flows into a hash digest from a module that is not a hash owner. |
| `warden/sha256-over-json-stringify` |  | Disallow a hash digest over JSON.stringify output, whose pre-image depends on object key order. |

## Import fences: `no-restricted-imports`

`pnpm lint` fails when a file imports a specifier in a group below. An override that does not restate a group allows that group in its files.

| Specifiers | Allowed in | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@ai-sdk/*` | `packages/ai/src/**` | Provider packages are owned by @warden/ai. Get a model from getBossModel() / getWorkerStrongModel() / getWorkerCheapModel() instead (docs/conventions.md, ADR-0006). |

## Overrides

Each entry in `overrides` changes the rules for its files. A later entry wins over an earlier one, so the order is the config order. The reason is the comment above the entry's `files` key.

| Files | Off | On | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/env/src/**` | `node/no-process-env` |  | The env owner reads process.env by definition. |
| `packages/ai/src/**` | `no-restricted-imports` |  | The provider owner. |
| `**/scripts/**`, `.claude/hooks/**` | `no-console`, `node/no-process-env` |  | Smoke scripts, probes, evals and repo tooling: they print to the terminal and set up child-process environments directly. |
| `**/*.mjs`, `**/*.js`, `**/*.cjs` | `typescript/no-unsafe-argument`, `typescript/no-unsafe-assignment`, `typescript/no-unsafe-call`, `typescript/no-unsafe-member-access`, `typescript/no-unsafe-return` |  | The no-unsafe-* family stays off ON PURPOSE for JavaScript sources, as in alfred. The gate scripts are JSDoc-typed `.mjs` checked with `noImplicitAny: false` (scripts/tsconfig.json), and `.claude/hooks/*.mjs` are in no tsconfig at all, so an unannotated binding, a parsed manifest, or a Node global is `any` there by construction. On 2026-10-20 the family reported 294 such reads in `.mjs`, none of them an escaped boundary. TypeScript sources everywhere, scripts included, keep all five rules on. |

## Files that lint does not read

`ignorePatterns` in `.oxlintrc.json`. No lint rule reaches these files.

| Pattern | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `**/.warden/**` | Warden's per-repo cache and run state, not source. |
| `**/migrations/**` | Drizzle migrations, generated by `pnpm db:generate`. |
| `dist/**` | Build output, generated from the linted sources. |
| `scripts/oxlint/anti-slop/**` | Vendored verbatim; proven by `pnpm check:oxlint-plugin`, not by linting its source. |

## Compiler flags

Each flag below changes what `pnpm check-types` accepts. `true` and `false` are the values in the tsconfig. An empty cell means that the tsconfig does not set the flag, so the TypeScript default applies, or `strict` sets it.

| Flag | `packages/config/tsconfig.base.json` | `scripts/tsconfig.json` | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checkJs` |  | `true` | JavaScript files are type-checked, with JSDoc as their types. |
| `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` | `true` | `true` | An optional property `k?: T` does not accept an explicit `undefined`. Omit the key instead. |
| `forceConsistentCasingInFileNames` | `true` | `true` | An import whose casing differs from the file on disk is an error. |
| `isolatedModules` | `true` |  | Each file compiles alone, so a single-file transpiler gives the same output. |
| `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` | `true` | `true` | A `case` with statements that falls through to the next `case` is an error. |
| `noImplicitAny` |  | `false` | A binding whose type tsc cannot infer is an error, not an implicit `any`. |
| `noImplicitReturns` | `true` | `true` | A function that returns a value on one path returns one on every path. |
| `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` | `true` |  | An index read (`xs[i]`, `record[key]`) has the type `T \| undefined`. |
| `noUnusedLocals` | `true` |  | An unused local declaration is an error. |
| `noUnusedParameters` | `true` |  | An unused parameter is an error. A leading `_` keeps one on purpose. |
| `skipLibCheck` | `true` | `true` | When `true`, tsc does not type-check declaration files (`.d.ts`). |
| `strict` | `true` | `true` | Turns on the strict family: `noImplicitAny`, `strictNullChecks`, `strictFunctionTypes`, `useUnknownInCatchVariables` and the rest. |
| `verbatimModuleSyntax` | `true` |  | An import used only as a type says `type`, and the emitted imports match the source. |

Each program below runs in `pnpm check-types`. A program that extends `@warden/config/tsconfig.base.json` gets its flags from the base.

| tsconfig | Extends |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/web/tsconfig.json` | `astro/tsconfigs/strict` |
| `packages/ai/tsconfig.json` | `@warden/config/tsconfig.base.json` |
| `packages/cli/tsconfig.json` | `@warden/config/tsconfig.base.json` |
| `packages/core/tsconfig.json` | `@warden/config/tsconfig.base.json` |
| `packages/db/tsconfig.json` | `@warden/config/tsconfig.base.json` |
| `packages/env/tsconfig.json` | `@warden/config/tsconfig.base.json` |
| `packages/mcp/tsconfig.json` | `@warden/config/tsconfig.base.json` |
| `scripts/tsconfig.json` | nothing |

## Check scripts

Each script below runs in `pnpm check`, in CI (`.github/workflows/check.yml`), or in both. The summary is the first comment paragraph of the script file, when the script runs one.

| Script | `pnpm check` | CI | Command | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `check-types` | no | yes | `turbo run check-types && tsc -p scripts/tsconfig.json` |  |
| `check:osv-cache` | yes | yes | `pnpm --filter @warden/cli smoke:osv-cache` | Checks the OSV cache against a real temporary SQLite database: malformed JSON, invalid records and expired rows refetch, and a valid row reuses the cache. Only the HTTP boundary is replaced, so the check needs no network and no credentials. |
| `check:oxlint-plugin` | yes | yes | `node scripts/check-oxlint-plugin.mjs` | Fails when a rule in one of the repo's oxlint JS plugins is untested, unregistered, unconfigured, or configured at "error" but not actually enforced by the root config. |
| `check:rules-catalog` | yes | yes | `node scripts/enforced-rules-catalog.mjs --check` | Writes docs/enforced-rules.md, the catalog of every rule that a gate enforces, from the files that define those rules. With `--check` it writes nothing and fails when the committed catalog differs from what the sources produce now. |
| `format:check` | yes | yes | `oxfmt --check --ignore-path .gitignore apps packages scripts .claude package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml turbo.json .oxlintrc.json .oxfmtrc.json` |  |
| `knip` | yes | yes | `knip --treat-config-hints-as-errors` |  |
| `lint` | yes | yes | `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json --deny-warnings` |  |
